quest.title: The Wind Settles
quest.description: Ayato claims that your job is done and that all that remains is to wait for the Kanjou Commission's internal reaction. Will things really proceed as he thinks they will?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x550, Primogem x60, Mora x31125, Guide to Elegance x5, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: These people from the Tenryou Commission have been here for days now.

dialogues.speaker: Kaede
dialogues.text: I guess they're here to pick up Lady Hiiragi... but why would it be taking so long?

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: I heard that the Kanjou Commission suddenly said they don't want Lady Hiiragi to leave.

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: To be honest, I'd be hesitant if I were her. A crowd this size comes to Ritou? Who knows what they could be planning.

dialogues.speaker: Kaede
dialogues.text: Shh! Stay quiet. Someone might hear you.

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: Oh, right, sorry. Ugh, how did things get to this point...

talks.objective: Go to Ritou to check on the situation

dialogues.speaker: Kaede
dialogues.text: I hope this is all resolved soon.

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: I know, right? What the heck is the Kanjou Commission doing...

talks.objective: Talk to the people of Ritou
Talk to the people of Ritou

dialogues.speaker: Yasuaki
dialogues.text: How much longer does your Master plan to hold them off...

dialogues.speaker: Hideo
dialogues.text: I have no idea. We're stuck in limbo here.

dialogues.speaker: Hideo
dialogues.text: Master's been very on edge these past few days. He gets irate over the smallest things and is suspicious of everything... He's been yelling at me a lot...

dialogues.speaker: Hideo
dialogues.text: I understand that he's anxious, but I mean... what can we do? I've told him before — never cross the Yashiro Commissioner.

dialogues.speaker: Yasuaki
dialogues.text: Yeah, good advice... With him, you just know that whatever he's doing, a lot of preparation has gone into it.

dialogues.speaker: Yasuaki
dialogues.text: If Lady Hiiragi is really taken away, then what will the Tenryou Commission do? And what will the Yashiro Commission do...

dialogues.speaker: Hideo
dialogues.text: Maybe we should tell Master to discuss things with Lady Hiiragi.

talks.objective: Talk to the people of Ritou

dialogues.speaker: Hatanaka
dialogues.text: Hello, how may I help?

response.speaker: Hatanaka
response.text: We arrived here two days ago to escort Lady Hiiragi to Inazuma City.

response.speaker: Hatanaka
response.text: Sir Kujou Kamaji gave us very strict orders, so we have to obey. But every time we attempt to receive the bride, the Hiiragi Clan always finds an excuse to delay things.

response.speaker: Hatanaka
response.text: Since we haven't fulfilled our duties yet... we decided to stay in Ritou until Lady Hiiragi is ready to come with us.

response.speaker: Hatanaka
response.text: We apologize, it was not our intention to stay here so long.

response.speaker: Hatanaka
response.text: We promise our presence here will not impact ordinary people's lives. We can only hope that the leaders of the Hiiragi Clan will start to cooperate soon.

response.speaker: Hatanaka
response.text: If this stalemate continues, who knows... Sir Kujou might give us orders to be less accommodating...

choices.text: Why is there such a strong Tenryou Commission presence here?

dialogues.speaker: Hatanaka
dialogues.text: Whatever happens, please don't worry. We know where to draw the line.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: Oh, Traveler!

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: I assume you've heard about everything that's been going on out there? What on earth is happening?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we can explain everything. So, what happened was—

choices.text: Hold on, someone might be eavesdropping.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You make sure that no one is eavesdropping before explaining the whole situation to Hiiragi Chisato.

response.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
response.text: After the Tenryou Commission arrived, they suddenly became alarmed. They keep having secretive discussions and won't allow me to have any direct contact with the Tenryou Commission.

response.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
response.text: I never would have thought that... this was Sir Kamisato's plan... Now it all makes sense.

response.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
response.text: ...I'm sorry, I haven't.

response.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
response.text: "Maybe there's no right or wrong decision... maybe everything would be easier if I simply didn't have a choice"...

response.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
response.text: I used to tell myself things like this to avoid having to think about it. But once I saw the notices appearing out of nowhere on the streets, signaling that the wedding was confirmed...

response.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
response.text: I didn't feel reassured at all. Instead, I felt a great sense of regret.

response.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
response.text: I keep thinking back to what Sir Kamisato said. This is supposed to be my bright and beautiful future... but what if it's not?

choices.text: This is exactly what he is worried about.

response.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
response.text: I can happily accept that if someone was trying to take advantage of my marriage, I should absolutely refuse to go through with it...

response.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
response.text: But that's not the answer I'm looking for. And also... now that things have escalated to this point, it will be tricky to resolve...

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: Ah, Lady Hiiragi, here you are. You scared me for a second. I thought you'd gone missing...

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: You... Wait, you're the ones who were with the Yashiro Commissioner that day!

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: What do you think you're doing here? Are you trying to convince Lady Hiiragi to leave!?

response.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
response.text: Calm down. They're my friends. They're just here to visit me.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: Friends? Are you sure? Just friends?

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: Lady Hiiragi, I told you already, these are exceptional circumstances. You need to be more vigilant in everything you do.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: You are extremely important to us and to the entire Kanjou Commission...

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: Who's to say... they don't have a hidden agenda?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you wanna accuse us of trying to abduct her, just come out and say it!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're acting far less dignified than when we last met.

response.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
response.text: Don't be rude. You've been very highly strung lately, seeing everything as a threat.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: I... Ugh...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You won't even follow Lady Hiiragi's orders now?

response.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
response.text: #Listen to me. I know all the ins and outs of everything that's happened so far. {F#Her}{M#His} arrival might well be your very last chance to fix this.

response.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
response.text: The present state of affairs in Ritou shows me that the situation has escalated well past the point where you could hope to control it. If this deadlock continues any longer, we will have nothing to gain and much to lose.

response.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
response.text: This is not an order. All I need you to do is give me an explanation and take responsibility for the situation.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: Understood, my lady. I shall discuss with the others right away.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good job, Chisato! You handled that well!

response.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
response.text: I was so nervous. But I thought, things are now so critical that I should at least give it a try... and it worked remarkably well.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's what I call a voice of authority.

response.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
response.text: Yes, well, let's wait and see what happens. I hope they provide a satisfactory response.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: A while later, Matsuura comes back with his tail between his legs.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: We had a serious discussion and reflected on our mistakes.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: In all honesty... no one can handle the weight of the situation here. Everyone is besides themselves with worry. It'll drive us mad if it continues any longer.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: Ah! I'm so sorry, my actions were radical and duplicitous, I was selfish and ignored the greater good, and then I left the situation to fester...

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: Would you... would you please give us a second chance? For my lady's sake, please, give the Kanjou Commission another chance...

choices.text: It's no use talking to me.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: I suppose you're right...

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: The only person who can change the Tenryou Commission's mind will be the Yashiro Commissioner.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: We'll head off to the Kamisato Estate shortly, and beseech him to help us with the utmost sincerity.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: Lady Hiiragi, might I ask you to join us? You are the most important person... Without you, we have no other way...

choices.text: You'll have to talk to Kamisato Ayato.
You can't rush into important things.

talks.objective: Meet and talk to Hiiragi Chisato
Go to the Kamisato Estate to meet Ayato

dialogues.speaker: Okabayashi
dialogues.text: Don't worry, the negotiations with the Kanjou Commission should be coming to an end very soon.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: Yashiro Commissioner, I'm sure you've heard the news... The Tenryou Commission has now occupied Ritou, refusing to leave until we hand Lady Hiiragi over to them.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: I realize I've greatly offended you with my atrocious actions, and I realize also that this must sound like the very height of absurdity, but please... have mercy, good sir...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Matsuura, I'm exceptionally busy, and have but a moment to spare before my next engagement. I fear this leaves no time for small talk.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: So please, if you would be so kind, get straight to the point.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: I know our apology means nothing to you, but we really have nothing else left to offer by this point. I'm terribly sorry... Everyone in the entire Kanjou Commission now realizes the gravity of this situation.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: Lady Hiiragi is indispensable to us. We promise to always support her.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: So, would it be at all possible for you to talk to Sir Kujou once more, on our behalf?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: You make it sound so easy. The Tri-Commission will be ridiculed by the public if we choose to withdraw the notices now and eat our words. What do you plan to do about this?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: To lose face for the Tri-Commission is to bring shame to Her Excellency. Are you and your associates ready to face the thunderous wrath of the Almighty Shogun?

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: We... We'll take full responsibility. We'll publish a new notice and hold a conference to explain the situation. We will make sure that the public knows this was all a huge misunderstanding.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: We'll do everything we can to minimize the impact, everything we can...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: ...Master Matsuura, you should have known it would come to this. Whatever were you thinking?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: But the Tri-Commission must always put the interests of Inazuma first, regardless of what Sir Kujou and I may feel at this present moment.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: If the situation in Ritou is left to fester any further, things may get out of control. But Lady Hiiragi and the inhabitants of Ritou are innocent.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: If we fail to contain the situation promptly, the rumor mill will wreak havoc on the Tri-Commission's reputation.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Try keeping a pet bird, you'll see what I mean. Songbirds who know how to hold a tune can be very pleasant to listen to, but they can also become irritating if they don't know when to stop.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: And as for the ones with excessively long tongues, well they're so insufferable that they can't be kept as pets at all... But it doesn't take a moment to cut out their tongues and silence them for good.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: ...Y—Yes... I understand!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I've listened to your concerns, and I'll talk to Sir Kujou for you. But I can't guarantee that he will change his mind.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: I understand. Thank you for your help, Yashiro Commissioner!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Alright, you ought to return now. I'm sure you have a sizable mess to deal with back in the Kanjou Commission?

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: Okay, then please excuse me... Thank you once again, Commissioner!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Ah yes, Lady Hiiragi, I have something to tell you. Would you mind?

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: Oh? Why, of course...

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: Sir Kamisato, you became a completely different person just now. It felt so intense.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Unruly servants like him need to be severely reprimanded. As a commissioner, the Almighty Shogun trusts me to do her will. I did as I should.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: But now I'd like to take off my commissioner hat and share a personal story with you.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: Oh, please. I'd love to hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: You must've heard that the Kamisato Clan once went through an extremely difficult period.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: My father worked incredibly hard to compensate for the grave errors made by the Kamisato Clan long ago and restore our reputation. The work took a toll on his health, and ultimately led to his untimely demise.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: My mother loved him dearly. She passed soon after.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: This sudden turn of events dealt a heavy blow to the Yashiro Commission. Behind the scenes, things became very unstable.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Everyone thought that the Kamisato Clan had lost power. That made my sister and me nothing but burdens hindering the ambitions of others.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: It may sound preposterous now, but I assure you that is the truth of what the Yashiro Commission has been through.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, pretty similar to how the Kanjou Commission is now...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Back then, I had no choice but to accept the position I was in. While I desperately looked around for powerful supporters, I endured smear campaigns and attempts to exploit me.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I had no other choice. I had to honor my parents' dying wishes, and I also had a young sister to take care of.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I didn't mind what became of me, but my family... No one can ever be allowed to trample over my precious family.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Fortunately, I persisted, and the Kamisato Clan was able to survive this storm.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: ...I think I now know where my sense of loss and confusion was coming from.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: Shinnojou once told me that he saw what was in me, in a way that no one else did... That's why he couldn't bear to see me live the rest of my life depending on someone else...

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: I thought the reason I felt unsettled was because of uncertainty over getting married. But the fact is, it's because I felt too young and inexperienced to handle the situation facing me.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: The reason why Sir Kujou was able to face the prospect of marriage so confidently is because he's prepared for anything.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: ...That's it. The situation I'm facing now is the same one he faced back then.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: When his clan was in crisis, he bravely drew his blade and challenged the Almighty Shogun. And now...

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: It is time for me to make a stand, and become my own person.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Well said. I'm sure once you have grown and gained confidence, your father will be able to let go and allow you to decide how you want to live the rest of your life.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: It might not sound exciting, but this kind of personal growth is a necessary step in the pursuit of true happiness.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: ...And I'm sure I can get there.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: I will use this as an opportunity to take over the responsibilities of the Hiiragi Clan. I'll think about marriage again after everything is more settled.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: This puts less pressure on Kamaji, and means I can support and protect myself without having to worry about becoming a burden or dependent on someone else.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: My best wishes to both of you were and remain heartfelt. When the time comes for the wedding to go ahead, I will come to congratulate you once more.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: Thank you, Sir Kamisato. I am grateful for everything you have shared with me.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: Now, if you'll excuse me, I have a lot to deal with back home.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Take care, Lady Hiiragi. I'm confident that on your return, you will find your Kanjou Commission associates most receptive to your instruction.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: Yes, in fact my recent experience suggests the same. Thank you once again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She really has the air of a leader now.

choices.text: She has a lot in common with Kamaji.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hats off to you too, sir! Everyone thought there was no way out until you pulled that super smart strategy out of nowhere!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: In fact, counter checking is a perfectly common maneuver in the game of chess.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Our rival this time was easy to deal with. He was smart, but short-sighted, and sloppy in his execution. This outcome is entirely within my expectation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even so... Paimon could never come up with a plan that cunning in a whole lifetime!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, it's kind of a relief to see that Chisato has decided to set the Hiiragi Clan straight.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I agree. Stability in Inazuma benefits me, as well. I wasn't about to pass up an opportunity to make less trouble for myself.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Hahaha, well, the fact is that I am first and foremost the Yashiro Commissioner.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Perhaps for Master Matsuura, power is his life's pursuit. But for me, nothing matters more than the stability of Inazuma.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: A stable nation is the prerequisite for a stable Yashiro Commission. Only then can the Kamisato Clan and the other Yashiro Commission clans have a peaceful existence.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: But human desire will always be a factor in the equation. This is not the first situation of its kind, nor will it be the last.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: All I have tried to do is make sure the three parties to the Tri-Commission serve to restrain each other. Stasis is not the only form of stability. A balance of power leaving no room for maneuver achieves the same end.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Another positive outcome is that everyone recognizes how important Lady Hiiragi is now. I think I did her a sizable favor in that regard.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Dealing with the Hiiragi Clan will be much easier for her than navigating a new and unfamiliar one.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whew, there were so many things at play over this one wedding...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Wait a second, you weren't trying to stop the wedding from the very beginning, were you!?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Hmm? I thought straight away it was bad timing. Nevertheless, everything I said to Hiiragi Chisato was entirely sincere.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: If you choose to give up your stance on something once, you'll be having to compromise for the rest of your life.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I didn't want to see her suffer because she didn't realize what she was getting into.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Now, she has the chance to become her own person. Let's see who she becomes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay then, guess we'll have to wait and see...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: See you next time.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Alright, farewell and profuse thanks to you both. I shall have to host you at the Kamisato Estate when my sister is next available.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Looks like everything's resolved.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Masterfully done, everything was perfect. Well, except for one minor detail... I somehow ended up with a glass of very peculiar-tasting milk.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Hmm? Didn't you like it? I distinctly remember you saying you are quite partial to exotic flavors.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Oh, my lord...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: The Traveler had one of those as well.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: #I'm sure {F#she's}{M#he's} made a great impression on you.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: #The Traveler did indeed play a critical role in this case. I'm sure both families would have been more guarded against me had {F#she}{M#he} and {F#her}{M#his} companion not been present.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: It wouldn't have been so easy to get to the heart of the matter.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: There you go again, my lord. Placing the focus on other people while discreetly performing your job to perfection.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Naturally. Ah yes, now that we're both free, let's finish off that game of chess we started a few days ago.

choices.text: You weren't in this just to help Chisato, were you?
They really are a good match for each other.

dialogues.speaker: Ide
dialogues.text: Sorry for the disruption. We're still waiting for further orders.

dialogues.speaker: Okabayashi
dialogues.text: Our duty here is to ensure the safety of this road.

dialogues.speaker: Okabayashi
dialogues.text: You'll see more Tenryou Commission members as you go further along. We're all here for the same duty. Please don't be alarmed.

dialogues.speaker: Hatanaka
dialogues.text: Everything is safe and sound. No unusual activity.

dialogues.speaker: Hatanaka
dialogues.text: Please feel free to go about your business. Our duty here should not affect you in any way.

dialogues.speaker: Ide
dialogues.text: What could be so urgent...

dialogues.speaker: Ide
dialogues.text: Oh, uh, don't mind me. Just talking to myself.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Hmm... What's with all these people coming in and out? And why does everyone look so serious?

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Maybe I should head home early today...

dialogues.speaker: Shogunate Announcement
dialogues.text: Ever may the Euthymia stand, long may the lightning shine. We are honored to hereby announce this most auspicious clime:

dialogues.speaker: Shogunate Announcement
dialogues.text: Sir Kujou Kamaji, Proxy Clan Head of the Tenryou Commission,

dialogues.speaker: Shogunate Announcement
dialogues.text: And Lady Hiiragi Chisato, Proxy Clan Head of the Kanjou Commission,

dialogues.speaker: Shogunate Announcement
dialogues.text: Shall be getting married in the near future.

dialogues.speaker: Yasuaki
dialogues.text: What's your Master thinking?

dialogues.speaker: Hideo
dialogues.text: Ugh, with his temper, it's hard to say...

dialogues.speaker: Yokoyama
dialogues.text: Please leave. Due to an ongoing emergency, we are receiving no guests at present except where a special invitation is given.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hiiragi Chisato is now at the center of every conversation in Ritou.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By now, the Kanjou Commission probably knows how important she is... but what about what she thinks?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go and see.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: By the way, aren't you a good friend of the Yashiro Commissioner?

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: Please put in some good words for me.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Actually, I don't think there's much point continuing that game... I'm pretty sure I don't have a chance of winning.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Hehe, well, I've forgotten where we left off amidst the activity of the past few days. Don't you want to take this opportunity to try and best me for once?

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: If you say so... alright, I'll give it my best shot!
